resources.string: AgePony stores your keys, recipients, and notes in a vault sealed on this device. Unlock it with biometrics, a password, or both.

AgePony stores your keys, recipients, and notes in a vault sealed on this device. No screen lock is set up, so protect it with a password or PIN. To unlock with a fingerprint instead, set up a screen lock in Android settings first, then create the vault.
Choose a password or PIN to unlock AgePony. There is no recovery if you forget it: the vault is sealed with it.
Unlock your vault to access your keys and notes.
Confirm your device PIN, pattern, or password to unlock.
No device PIN, pattern, or password is set.
Too many wrong attempts. Try again in %1$s.
Forgot it? Open without the PIN
Forgot it? Open without the password

Until this update, No lock opened the vault without asking for the PIN. This opens it that way one more time and removes the PIN, so the vault stays on No lock with nothing to confirm. You can set a new one in Settings.

Until this update, No lock opened the vault without asking for the password. This opens it that way one more time and removes the password, so the vault stays on No lock with nothing to confirm. You can set a new one in Settings.
Just need a passphrase? Continue without unlocking
Confirm your PIN, pattern, or password
This security key needs a PIN. Enter it below and sign again.
Produces a detached signature saved as its own small file next to the original. Send both; the file itself is not changed or encrypted.
No signing keys in your vault yet. Add an SSH key, a hardware key, or a security key under Identities first.
Hold your security key against the back of the phone…
Signing in the device\'s secure hardware…
Send the signature file along with the original. Signatures are scoped to AgePony\'s namespace; to check one on the command line:
No signers found in that file.
Signatures from these keys verify with the name you gave them. The list imports from and exports to an OpenSSH signers file (allowed_signers), the one ssh-keygen -Y verify reads.
A trusted signer is someone else\'s public key that you\'ve checked, so their signatures show their name. Add one below, import a signers file, or add the signer from a verify result.
That doesn\'t look like an SSH public key line.
That key is already on the list.
Signatures from this key will verify as valid but unknown instead of carrying this name.
Tick the signers to trust. Files signed by a trusted signer show as signed by that name.
An SSH public key line, like the contents of an id_ed25519.pub.
A recipient saved for encryption isn\'t trusted for signatures yet. Pick one to add its key to your trusted signers.
That doesn\'t look like an SSH signature.
Pick the file first, then its signature (the .sig that came with it). The file is only read, never changed.
The key belongs to \"%1$s\" on your trusted signers list. %2$s
Its entry doesn\'t allow this signature.
Valid signature, signer not in your vault
The math checks out, but this key isn\'t one of yours and isn\'t on your trusted signers list. If you know whose it is, add it so future signatures carry their name.
The signature doesn\'t match this file.
The signature is damaged or isn\'t an SSH signature.
This signature was made for something else (namespace %1$s).
The signer\'s RSA key isn\'t one AgePony accepts: it\'s too small, too large or has an unusual exponent.
The signature was made without touching the security key, so it doesn\'t count.
The signature doesn\'t match this file.
Its entry has options AgePony can\'t read.
Its entry has options AgePony doesn\'t support: %1$s.
Its entry is a certificate authority, which AgePony doesn\'t support.
Its entry doesn\'t allow the namespace \"%1$s\".
Its entry requires a touch on the security key.
Its entry requires a PIN or biometric check on the security key.
Its entry doesn\'t allow this signature.
Name the person or system this key belongs to.
A note is text kept encrypted with its own passphrase, apart from your keys. Only someone who knows the passphrase can read it.
scrypt work factor 2^18 makes brute force expensive, but a guessable passphrase is still guessable. There\'s no recovery if you forget it.
Not enough memory to encrypt this note on this device.
Not enough memory to decrypt this note.
Not enough memory to save this note.
Unsaved changes. Tap Save to re-encrypt.
Your vault stays locked. Nothing here can see your keys, recipients or notes.
Text to encrypt, or an armored age block to decrypt
Not enough memory for this passphrase\'s work factor on this device.
AgePony encrypts files, text, and notes with the modern age encryption standard. Everything happens right here on your device.
An identity is your personal keypair. The private key is sealed in your vault and never leaves this device. Create one on the Identities tab to start encrypting.
Add recipients by their public key or GitHub username. Encrypt to one person or many at once, and to yourself so you can always open your own files.
Encrypt and decrypt files from the Files tab, encrypt short messages on the Text tab, and keep private notes locked behind your vault.
AgePony has no accounts, no servers and no tracking. Your vault is sealed on this device and opened only by biometrics, your device PIN or a password. Your keys and your data stay with you.
Enter your security key PIN to authorize signing.
Point the camera at a QR code containing an age recipient or SSH public key.
Camera access is needed to scan QR codes.
The app you selected this in only lets AgePony read the text, not change it. Copy the result and paste it back over your selection.
Unlock your vault with biometrics or your PIN.
Unlock your vault with biometrics or your password.
The phone\'s screen lock doesn\'t open AgePony.
A fingerprint or face was added or removed, so biometrics stopped opening AgePony. Confirm with biometrics now to unlock with them again. Until then, only your app password or PIN opens the vault.
A fingerprint or face was added or removed on this phone.

A fingerprint or face was added or removed on this phone since the vault was locked to biometrics, so AgePony asks for your PIN here instead. If you didn\'t change this yourself, check your phone\'s security settings for a fingerprint or face you didn\'t add before you enter your PIN.

A fingerprint or face was added or removed on this phone since the vault was locked to biometrics, so AgePony asks for your password here instead. If you didn\'t change this yourself, check your phone\'s security settings for a fingerprint or face you didn\'t add before you enter your password.
Biometrics aren\'t available right now, so AgePony asks for your PIN instead. The phone\'s screen lock is never used for this.
Biometrics aren\'t available right now, so AgePony asks for your password instead. The phone\'s screen lock is never used for this.
AgePony can\'t confirm it\'s you right now, because neither biometrics nor the screen lock can be used. Try again in a moment.
The text decrypted, but the signed bundle inside it is damaged.
